sentences.l2: 数据可视化的核心并不在于图表是否美观，而在于能否让读者迅速把握信息的要义。
sentences.l1: The core of data visualization lies not in whether a chart is attractive, but in whether it lets readers quickly grasp the essence of the information.

sentences.l2: 选择图表之前，首先应明确自己想表达什么。
sentences.l1: Before choosing a chart, you should first be clear about what you want to express.

sentences.l2: 倘若要比较不同类别之间的差异，例如各部门的季度销售额，柱状图最为直观，因为人眼对柱子高度的差别格外敏感。
sentences.l1: If you want to compare the differences between categories, such as the quarterly sales of each department, a bar chart is the most intuitive, because the human eye is especially sensitive to differences in the height of bars.

sentences.l2: 倘若要呈现数据随时间变化的趋势，例如某城市一年来的气温起伏，折线图则更为合适，连续的线条能够清晰地展现上升与下降的走向。
sentences.l1: If you want to present the trend of data changing over time, such as a city's temperature fluctuations over a year, a line chart is more suitable, and a continuous line can clearly show the direction of rises and falls.

sentences.l2: 至于饼图，它适用于表现各部分占整体的比例，但类别一旦超过五六个，扇形就会显得拥挤，读者难以分辨。
sentences.l1: As for the pie chart, it is suited to showing the proportion each part makes up of the whole, but once there are more than five or six categories, the slices will look crowded and readers will find it hard to tell them apart.

sentences.l2: 此外，无论采用哪种图表，都要标注清楚坐标轴的名称与单位，并避免截断坐标轴来夸大差距，否则容易误导观众。
sentences.l1: In addition, whichever chart you use, you must clearly label the names and units of the axes, and avoid truncating the axis to exaggerate differences, otherwise it easily misleads the audience.
